rationale: M59 (#825). Every line below is the line the CALL is written on in callsite-lines-825.scala, read off the source, not off analyzer output. The fixture exists because a call_expression starts at its RECEIVER, so a multi-line chain used to stamp every call in the chain with the opening line: on the real cats-effect Example.scala, `.as(ExitCode(2))` written on line 23 was reported on line 22, and on a 300-file scala3 sample that mechanism put 330 of 7,517 landed lines in the wrong place. The forbidRelationships entries are the load-bearing half — they are the pre-fix behaviour, so re-introducing the receiver-start line fails the gate instead of silently passing.

forbidRelationships.note: the pre-fix defect: `.as(...)` is on line 13, reported on the chain-opening line 12
same mechanism on a newline-continued chain: `.filter` is on line 18, the receiver opens on line 16
